content:
A question that arises from time to time is how to ensure that a code action or syntax linter is available throughout an entire project. To my knowledge, nothing exists to do so out of the box. The pattern that existing projects use is to create a module with these imports, usually called Init, and then check that this is transitively imported in every other file. My understanding is this pattern started in Mathlib, and has subsequently been adopted by other developments like Iris-Lean and CSLib, each with their own method of checking transitive imports. This adds additional friction for users wanting to use code actions or linters (recent example: #batteries > importing `Batteries.CodeAction` project-wide). Even in experienced libraries, PRs like #44387 reveal situations where a linter is accidentally not as widely imported as one would expect when this is managed implicitly via transitive imports.

I would like to propose that that this be added as functionality provided via a new option lake shake --ensure-imports <MODULES>. The idea would be that you pass a list of modules, it determines locations further down the import graph missing these imports (avoiding cycles), and suggests adding all of these imports. The idea that shake might be the appropriate place for this was suggested at #general > Customizing prelude for automatic imports? @ 💬 by @Sebastian Ullrich. I think this is a relatively small addition that would make the adoption of code actions and linters much easier, especially downstream of Mathlib.

I wanted to post here before opening an RFC issue to see if this is more complex than I am realizing, any details I've neglected, or if there are other proposed solutions entirely.
I created lean4#15593. The same idea as here, though I mentioned that you might want to do this via module -- shake comments.

I tried it out from the PR toolchain and this looks great to me! I thought for a while about allowing one versus multiple modules and ultimately agree that just one is both much simpler to implement and probably better downstream for a variety of reasons.
